study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative models pre-trained on cross-sectional data to evaluate intra-individual longitudinal changes in neuroimaging data

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study utilizes pre-trained Warped Bayesian Linear Regression (WBLR) normative models. Specifically, they used the 'lifespan_58K_82_sites' pre-trained model from the PCNtoolkit, which was trained on 58,836 participants across 82 sites. The WBLR model includes a warping function φ(y) to accommodate non-Gaussian errors and B-spline basis expansion for non-linear relationships.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We utilise the Warped Bayesian Linear Regression normative model [3] as a basis for our work.; The pre-trained model used for adaptation was the lifespan_58K_82_sites [10].; In this form, the original models were fit on a large dataset consisting of 58,836 participants scanned across 82 sites.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: RehakBuckova2025.pdf.md: Section 1 Introduction / Section 2.3 Preprocessing and Analysis

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled cortical thickness and subcortical volumes as the response variables. These were derived from T1-weighted MRI images preprocessed using FreeSurfer (v7.2) recon-all pipeline, with both longitudinal and cross-sectional preprocessing approaches evaluated.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Specifically, cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were modelled, and the models were validated against a subset of 24,000 participants, the quality of which were was checked manually [10].; Prior to normative modelling, all T1 images were preprocessed using the Freesurfer v.(7.2) recon-all pipeline.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: RehakBuckova2025.pdf.md: Section 2.1.1 Original model for cross-sectional data / Section 2.3 Preprocessing and Analysis

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model uses age and sex as demographic covariates, with site effects accommodated through site dummy variables. The model uses B-spline basis expansion for age to capture non-linear relationships. The pre-trained model was trained on data from 82 different scanning sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: This framework models each image-derived phenotype (IDP) (e.g., voxel intensity, regional thickness, or regional volume) independently as a function of demographic or clinical variables (e.g., age, sex, scanning site) in a large healthy population.; To accommodate site-level effects, we append it with site dummies.; To capture non-linear relationships, we use a B-spline basis expansion of the original independent variables x_n
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: RehakBuckova2025.pdf.md: Section 1 Introduction / Section 2.1.1 Original model for cross-sectional data
